According to the AlphaFold prediction of the C-terminal tail, this could be because the last few residues of the C-terminus (F546, A547, W548, L549, R550 of DhcHACS) are located closer to the catalytic site. In contrast, RKPQQ residues that come before them cover the CoA moiety. Structural differences between ApbHACS and DhcHACS reveal keys to improving acyloin condensation activity. While DhcHACS has higher k and catalytic efficiency than ApbHACS towards cat formaldehyde, it also exhibits a higher K , which is undesirable given the toxic nature of M formaldehyde. To investigate the structural difference between the two proteins, we used the “Pairwise Structure Alignment” function on the Protein Data Bank (PDB) website (www.rcsb.org). ApbHACS and DhcHACS structures modeled by AlphaFold were used for structure comparison, and the result showed that two residues were not aligned between the two protein structures. An ApbHACS-DhcHACS hybrid protein was constructed by inserting or deleting a residue to align the two structures without gaps. As a result, ApbHACS N465ins, R493del, and N465ins R493del were engineered for “DhcHACS-like” ApbHACS whereas DhcHACS N461del, R480ins, and N461del R480ins were made for “ApbHACS-like” DhcHACS. While all three DhcHACS-like ApbHACS mutants showed decreased activities, ApbHACS-like DhcHACS showed significant improvement in activities, especially R480ins, with up to 38% increase in activity (Figure 27C). 40 We also explored an alternative approach intended to improve the formaldehyde binding affinity of DhcHACS by engineering the active site of DhcHACS to mimic ApbHACS. Comparing the active site residues of the two enzymes, residues in the TPP binding region are fully conserved, and the only nonmatching residues in the formyl-CoA binding region are A253, P254, and M276 of DhcHACS. Consequently, DhcHACS A253G P254G and DhcHACS M276I were constructed to mimic the active site of ApbHACS. Another target region was the c-terminal region, where ApbHACS and DhcHACS have nonmatching residues at the end, which were shown to be important for enzyme activity through alanine scanning (Figure 27B). Based on the predicted structure of ApbHACS and DhcHACS, the difference in C-termini shows a slightly different orientation of the closing loop. We hypothesized that this difference could contribute to the different formaldehyde binding affinity between ApbHACS and DhcHACS and constructed the following DhcHACS mutant using ApbHACS as a template: DhcHACS L549H T550G R551del. Mutations in the DhcHACS formyl-CoA binding region (A253G P254G) and C-terminus (L549H T550G R551del) showed significant improvement in the glycolate flux (Figure 27C). We also tried combining beneficial mutations and found that DhcHACS R480del L549H T550G R551del showed up to 50% improvement compared to the wildtype DhcHACS (Figure 27C).
